message.content:
I'm planning two features for KasirKu (Next.js 16 POS app, Android app wraps it in Capacitor WebView, kitchen/bar receipt printing via LAN sockets or Bluetooth dispatched from the CLIENT since Vercel serverless can't reach a shop's private LAN/Bluetooth):

1. A "reprint kitchen ticket" button for a PAST transaction (currently kitchen tickets only auto-print once, at checkout time — no way to resend if the printer was off or it just needs reprinting).
2. A retry mechanism so that if a kitchen/bar printer is off when a print job is attempted, the ticket still gets printed automatically once the printer comes back online, instead of being silently dropped (current behavior: best-effort, logs a failure via logKitchenPrintFailures, and that's it — no retry, no persistence).

I need you to report back (under 500 words) on the EXACT current state of the kitchen printing pipeline, since architecture may have changed across recent commits:

1. `src/lib/kitchen-print.ts` — what does `buildKitchenPrintJobs` do today (signature, inputs, what it queries, what it returns)? Does it still exist, or was it renamed/restructured?
2. `src/lib/dispatch-print-jobs.ts` — read the full file. How does `dispatchPrintJobs`/`dispatchOne` work today (LAN via print-agent HTTP relay, LAN/Bluetooth via native Capacitor plugin, web fallback)? What happens on failure today — is there ANY persistence/retry, or does it just report failure via `logKitchenPrintFailures`?
3. `src/app/business/[businessId]/pos/actions.ts` — find `checkout()` and `updateSelfOrderStatus()` (or wherever kitchen print jobs get built today) — confirm how they call `buildKitchenPrintJobs`/similar, and what data (product categories, items) feeds into it. Also check if there's a `buildTestPrintJob`-style action already, and any existing reprint-adjacent action.
4. `src/lib/offline-queue.ts` and `src/lib/offline-db.ts` — read fully. This is the existing IndexedDB-based retry-queue pattern used for offline checkout retry (pending_sales store). I want to know its exact shape (types, functions: enqueueSale, listPending, markSyncing, markSynced, markError, discardPending) so a NEW similar queue for failed print jobs can mirror this pattern consistently.
5. `src/hooks/use-offline-sync.ts` — read fully, this is the polling/retry hook for the sale queue (retries every 20s when pending exist, on 'online' event, etc). I want to replicate this pattern for print job retries.
6. Where does the transaction detail page live (`src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/transactions/[transactionId]/page.tsx` or similar) — what data does it already have available (transaction_items, categories) that a "reprint to kitchen/bar" button would need? Is `Capacitor.isNativePlatform()` already imported/used anywhere near there (e.g. for the "Cetak ke <printer>" receipt button pattern added recently)?
7. Check `kitchen_printers` table columns currently in use (grep migrations under supabase/migrations for "kitchen_printers") — confirm current columns (id, name, categories, connection_type, address, device_label, prints_receipt, anything else).

Report concrete facts with file paths and line numbers/snippets. Don't propose a design — I'll do that myself using your findings.

content.text:
Now I have everything needed.

## Report

**1. `src/lib/kitchen-print.ts`** — Exists, unchanged pattern. `buildKitchenPrintJobs(supabase: SupabaseClient, businessId: string, job: KitchenPrintJob): Promise<KitchenPrintJobPayload[]>` where `KitchenPrintJob = { source, label, items: (KitchenTicketItem & { category: string | null })[] }`. It queries `kitchen_printers` (`id, name, categories, connection_type, address, prints_receipt`) filtered `.eq("business_id", businessId)`, excludes rows with no `address` or `prints_receipt === true`, fans items out per printer by category match (empty `categories` array = catch-all), builds an ESC/POS buffer per matched printer via `buildKitchenTicket`, and returns `KitchenPrintJobPayload[]` (`printerName, address, connectionType, bytesBase64`). No persistence/retry logic here — pure builder.

**2. `src/lib/dispatch-print-jobs.ts`** — `"use client"` file. `dispatchOne(job)`: if `Capacitor.isNativePlatform()`, calls native `KitchenPrinter.printLan`/`printBluetooth` plugin; else if `connectionType === "bluetooth"` returns `{ok:false, reason:"printer_unreachable", error:"unsupported_on_web"}`; else falls back to `printViaAgent` (HTTP relay to print-agent). `dispatchPrintJobs(businessId, jobs)` runs all jobs via `Promise.all`, and on any failure calls `logKitchenPrintFailures(businessId, failed.map(...))` (fire-and-forget, `.catch(() => {})`) — this only writes an activity-log warning row via `logActivity`. **No queue, no persistence, no retry whatsoever** — failed jobs are simply logged and dropped. `dispatchReceiptThenKitchenJobs` awaits receipt jobs, then kitchen jobs, sequentially.

**3. `src/app/business/[businessId]/pos/actions.ts`**:
- `checkout()` (line 76): after RPC success, if `!already_existed`, runs `Promise.all([logActivity, buildKitchenPrintJobsForItems(...), buildReceiptPrintJobsForTransaction(...)])`. `buildKitchenPrintJobsForItems` (line 200) fetches `products.select("id, name, category")` for the item productIds, then calls `buildKitchenPrintJobs`, wrapped in `.catch(() => [])`. Returns `{ printJobs, receiptPrintJobs }` in `CheckoutResult`.
- `updateSelfOrderStatus()` (line 592): on `status === "diproses"`, queries `self_order_items` joined with `products(category)`, calls `buildKitchenPrintJobs` directly (also `.catch(() => [])`), returns `printJobs` in result.
- `logKitchenPrintFailures` (line 226): writes one `logActivity` "sistem"/"warning" row summarizing failed printer names + errors. That's its entire effect.
- `buildTestPrintJob(businessId, printerId)` (line 249) exists — single-printer, no category routing, builds a literal test ticket buffer, used by "Tes Cetak" screen. This is the closest existing pattern to a per-transaction reprint action.
- `buildReceiptPrintJob` (in `transactions/actions.ts`, not pos/actions.ts) builds one receipt job for one printer given a `transactionId` — reads `transaction_items`/`transaction_payments`/`transactions` via `buildReceiptBuffer`. This is analogous groundwork for a "reprint kitchen ticket for past transaction" action but currently only builds the *receipt* (priced) ticket, not a kitchen (unpriced, category-routed) ticket. `transaction_items` already stores `category` per line (selected in transaction detail page: `select("id, name, category, price, qty")`), so a reprint action could rebuild kitchen jobs straight from `transaction_items` without re-joining `products`.

**4/5. Offline queue (`offline-queue.ts`/`offline-db.ts`) and `use-offline-sync.ts`** — IndexedDB store `pending_sales` (keyPath `clientRef`, index `by-business`), DB `kasirku-offline` v2 (also has `pos_cache` store, unrelated). Types: `PendingSaleStatus = "pending"|"syncing"|"error"`; `PendingSale = PendingRetailSale | PendingTicketSale` (discriminated by `kind`), each carrying `clientRef, businessId, createdAt, status, errorMessage?, payload`. Functions: `enqueueSale`, `listPending(businessId)`, `markSyncing`, `markSynced(clientRef)`, `markError(sale, message)`, `discardPending(clientRef)`, plus `pendingStockDeltas`. `useOfflineSync(businessId)` hook: retries every 20s (`SYNC_INTERVAL_MS`) if `pending.length > 0`, on `window` `online` event, guarded by `syncingRef` to prevent overlap; skips rows already `status === "error"` (manual-review only, no auto-retry); sequential `for` loop (not parallel) per sale; on success dispatches kitchen/receipt jobs via `dispatchReceiptThenKitchenJobs`; on thrown error re-enqueues as `pending` for next cycle.

**6. Transaction detail page** — `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/transactions/[transactionId]/page.tsx`. Already fetches `transaction_items` (`id, name, category, price, qty`) and `transactions` core fields; no `Capacitor` import here (it's a pure server component, no print button). The `Capacitor.isNativePlatform()` + "Cetak ke <printer>" pattern lives in the sibling `receipt/print-button.tsx` (client component), which fetches `kitchen_printers.select("id, name")` in `receipt/page.tsx` and passes as props; `handlePrintToPrinter` calls `buildReceiptPrintJob` then `dispatchPrintJobs`. A reprint-kitchen-ticket button would follow this exact print-button.tsx pattern but needs categories per printer (currently `receipt/page.tsx` only selects `id, name` from `kitchen_printers`, not `categories`/`connection_type`/`address`/`prints_receipt`).

**7. `kitchen_printers` columns** — from `20260702100500_fnb_support_tables.sql` + 2 later migrations: `id uuid pk`, `business_id uuid fk`, `name text`, `categories text[] default '{}'`, `connection_type text check in ('bluetooth','lan') default 'bluetooth'`, `address text` (nullable), `device_label text` (added 20260726130000), `prints_receipt boolean default false` (added 20260727120000).
